title: Jack Works from Home
subtitle: No commute, no boss in the room — and nobody to have lunch with.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about working from home: the day, the good parts and the lonely parts.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: My husband Jack works from home. He is a web designer. He makes websites for small companies.
He starts at nine. His desk is in the bedroom, next to the window, with a computer, a big screen, and a cup of coffee that is always cold.
In the morning he has meetings on the computer. He wears a good shirt and old pants, because people only see the top half.
He has no boss in the room, so nobody tells him what to do. But he has nobody to talk to either, and some days he does not leave the apartment.
At one o'clock he has lunch alone. Then he works until six.
“Do you like it?” I ask him.
“I like the work,” he says. “I don't like the quiet.”
On Wednesday he takes his computer to a café. It is noisy and the coffee is expensive, but there are people, and he comes home happier.

a table for working or writing
the flat part of a computer you look at
a time when people talk about work together
to have clothes on your body
the clothes you wear on your legs — American; British say trousers
the part of you above the middle
the person who tells you what to do at work

He has lunch alone at one o'clock.

items.statement: Jack has a boss in the room with him.
items.explanation: False. “He does not have a boss in the room.”
